newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's STET looks to gain in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Italy's STET looks to gain in Spain.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled telecoms group STET on Monday launched its bid to be number two operator in the lucrative Spanish market and prevent itself being left out in the cold in a whirlwind of international alliances.

STET concluded a co-operative telecoms deal with Spanish electricity groups Endesa and Union Fenosa aimed at taking part in a privatisation bid for Retevision, the number two Spanish national telecoms operator.

But the bidding battle for a 60 percent stake in Retevision was immediately joined by a more internationally-spread consortium taking in French, German and U.S. telecom interests which analysts said appeared to be the favourite for success.

The competing consortium is between Spanish bank Banca Central Hispano, Spanish railway operator Renfe, France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and U.S. Sprint, the last three making up the Global One alliance.

But STET desperate for international success in the run up to its own privatisation and European telecoms liberalisation may be tempted to bid aggressively to secure success for its overseas expansion plans and compete head on with Spain's recently-privatised Telefonica de Espana SA.

"This could be seen as a forced move. STET has to be seen to be bidding for these types of businesses or it gets locked into its own market," said telecoms industry analyst Bill Coleman at HSBC James Capel in London.

The three-way partnership, owned 50.55 percent by Endesa, 30 percent by STET, and 19.45 percent by Union Fenosa, will utilise the Spanish groups' telecom fibre optic network of 10,000 km for immediate use as an alternative to Telefonica.

Analysts pointed out that Retevision is an attractive proposition with licences to operate a full range of services while the Spanish telecom market is fully liberalised at the end of 1998, one year later than the rest of the European Union.

STET's international aspirations have had success in Latin America while it has some interests in Europe outside Italy, but it failed in its bid to enter the Russian market and it is outside the three major world telecoms alliances.
These three include Global One, the British Telecom MCI Communications Concert alliance which now brings in Telefonica de Espana SA and Portugal Telecom, and the AT&T -led partnership Unisource.
"STET fears being left out in the cold and may be tempted to pay a high price to show it is serious about its international expansion," said another analyst with an Italian bank.

STET almost clinched a $1.4 billion deal to invest in the Russian market in December 1995, but the deal with Russia's second largest telecoms company Svyazinvest failed on details. Ironically, STET shares rose then on the relief the group would not be pouring money into an uncertain investment.
